column1: # The CENSUS — library routines worth a row and not measured yet (@PLN158 shape 1).
# Columns: library <TAB> routine <TAB> class <TAB> kind <TAB> rank <TAB> why a program spends time here <TAB> workload <TAB> the Rust twin
#   kind  loft = pure loft · native = a Rust cdylib does the work · mixed
#   rank  1 = the survey's first pick for its tree · 2 = a further candidate
# Surveyed 2026-09-21 from the published API (doc/claude/LIBRARIES.md) and the library
# sources; a row moves to routines.tsv the day its lane prints it.  Line numbers are the
# survey's, against the published package (~/.loft/registry) or the branch named there.

every word helper re-splits the line: a 12-field line is split a dozen times
interpolation and `+=` per side, called once per proposal in the recovery enumeration
a window sweep appending into FIVE parallel vectors, re-run by every surface routine
each of up to 24 trials allocates a fresh edge set, element by element into two vectors
up to 256 lattice steps, each solving 6 bisector intersections in doubles

column6: two full passes through four accessor families, then a halo pass of three calls per slot
one file-read builtin crossing PER CELL per section
a hash probe + insert per candidate, keyed on a freshly built text
twelve insertion sorts writing a growing vector in place
one sqrt plus two accessor calls per cell: the cleanest one-op-per-cell float lane
two full window sweeps of sqrt / atan2 per point per segment
a fresh set allocated and swept, then four reads and a write per boundary edge
a set allocated by a push loop, then written one cell at a time through an accessor

four file-append builtin crossings per filled cell
every word helper re-splits the line: a 12-field bone line is split ~15 times
